beats.intro: Slope intercept form needs the y intercept. [[q]]But often you know the slope and some other point. Point slope form is built for that.
beats.derive: Here's a line with slope m, through a known point, x one, y one. [[any]]Now take any other point on the line, x, y. [[rise]]From the known point, the rise is y minus y one. [[run]]The run is x minus x one. [[slope]]Rise over run is the slope, so y minus y one, over x minus x one, equals m. [[mult]]Multiply both sides by x minus x one, and you get point slope form: y minus y one equals m times x minus x one.
beats.read: Reading this form takes care with signs. [[ex]]Take y minus three equals two times x minus seven. [[m]]The slope is two. [[pt]]And the point is seven, three: the numbers being subtracted. [[ex2]]Now y plus one equals negative two times x minus nine. [[rew]]y plus one is y minus negative one, [[pt2]]so the point is nine, negative one, and the slope is negative two.
beats.q1: Quick check. Read the slope and the point.
beats.graph: To graph a line from a point and a slope, [[pt]]plot the point: here, negative one, four. [[st]]The slope is two, which is two over one: up two, right one. [[line]]Draw the line through both points. [[eq]]Its equation in point slope form is y minus four equals two times x plus one.
beats.q2: Quick check. Plot the point this equation names.
beats.twoPts: If you know two points, find the slope first. [[pts]]The points three, negative five and seven, one. [[m]]The slope is one minus negative five, over seven minus three: six fourths, or three halves. [[e1]]Using the point three, negative five: y plus five equals three halves times x minus three. [[e2]]Using seven, one instead: y minus one equals three halves times x minus seven. [[same]]Different equations, same line. Either one is correct.
beats.toSI: You can turn point slope form into slope intercept form. [[ex]]A line has slope negative two and passes through one, six. [[ps]]In point slope form: y minus six equals negative two times x minus one. [[dist]]Distribute the negative two: negative two x plus two. [[add]]Add six to both sides: y equals negative two x plus eight. [[chk]]The y intercept is eight.
beats.q3: Quick check. Write it in slope intercept form.
beats.standard: There's one more common form: [[f]]standard form, A x plus B y equals C. [[rule]]A, B, and C are integers, and A is positive. [[ex]]Take slope one third through negative twelve, seven. [[ps]]Point slope form gives y minus seven equals one third times x plus twelve. [[x3]]Multiply both sides by three to clear the fraction. [[mv]]Move the x term to the left: negative x plus three y equals thirty-three. [[neg]]A must be positive, so multiply everything by negative one: x minus three y equals negative thirty-three.
beats.q4: Quick check. Finish the standard form.
beats.wrap: Three forms, one line. [[w1]]Slope intercept: y equals m x plus b. [[w2]]Point slope: y minus y one equals m times x minus x one. Watch the signs when you read the point. [[w3]]Standard: A x plus B y equals C, with integers and a positive A. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
